newsitem.title: USA: IDT sees higher Q3 telecom revs. [CORRECTED 15:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: IDT sees higher Q3 telecom revs. [CORRECTED 15:00 GMT]

text.p: (Corrects headline and text to reflect that projection refers to telecom portion of revenues only, not total third quarter revenues.)
IDT Corp, an overseas long distance reseller, said Wednesday it signed a deal with Cable and Wireless Plc to route and terminate calls.
In a statement, IDT said it believed the Cable & Wireless deal to be the first of several upcoming larger carrier deals.
It said it expected telecom revenues for the quarter ending April 30 to show a significant gain over the previous quarter's telecom revenue of $21.9 million.
The company also said it has made major strides with its international network build-out, which should greatly boost gross margins on traffic running over the company's network.
IDT spokeswoman Sarah Hofstetter said the company expected telecom revenues for fiscal third quarter in the range of $25 million to $26 million, but "closer to $26 million."

The Cable and Wireless deal follows a similar operating deal with WorldCom Inc announced March 14. The spokeswoman said IDT expected to announce another deal with a large telecommunications network provider within two weeks.
The company said it has already started routing call minutes through C&W's network.
C&W is expected to route traffic through IDT's network beginning in June 1997, leading to an expected doubling of traffic by the end of IDT's fiscal year at July 31.
The deal was made possible because of a recent upgrade of IDT's switch to support SS7 signaling.
IDT routes and resells international long distance services to businesses in 131 countries. It has over 150,000 U.S. retail customers, it said.
